context: Letter-value (boxen) plot comparing five synthetic distributions (n=1000 each: symmetric, right-skewed, left-skewed, bimodal, heavy-tailed) with a chart/table toggle; nested boxes encode quantile depth via decreasing width and a sequential blue color ramp.
first_impression: Statistically sophisticated and honest — data-driven Y scale via d3.extent, correct width-decreasing convention for depth levels, and a keyed table join make this structurally sound.
what_works: Y scale domain is fully data-driven (d3.extent on all min/max values with proportional padding — no magic numbers); table data join uses a key function (d => d.id) ensuring object constancy across sorts.
what_doesnt: Outlier fence is selected by widest value range across all letter-value levels rather than the deepest level, which is fragile for pathological distributions where an inner level could span a wider numeric range; color domain maps depth-index 0 (Fourths) to darkest blue via domain([maxDepth,0]) but the visual is internally consistent with the legend, so this is a legibility choice not a deception.
